text.p: English champions Manchester United announced on Friday they have signed Tottenham and England striker Teddy Sheringham for a fee in the region of 3.5 million sterling ($5.8 million).
Ironically the England striker's first match for his new club could be against Spurs in next season's opener for both clubs at White Hart Lane on August 10.
Sheringham had requested a transfer from Spurs because he was unhappy that the London club do not regularly challenge for major honours.
Spurs were originally believed to have asked six million pounds ($10 million) for Sheringham but United were known to be wary of paying that much for a 31-year-old player.
It is the biggest signing by United during the close season following earlier unsuccessful bids for several players including Bayern United defender Marcus Babbel
Earlier during the close season, United lost French striker Eric Cantona when he unexpectedly announced his retirement.
